Laurĕŏlus , i, m.,
I.a notorious robber, who is said to have been crucified and torn to pieces by wild beasts; hero of a play by the mimographer Q. Lutatius Catulus, Juv. 8, 187; Mart. Spect. 7; Suet. Calig. 57.
From A Latin Dictionary (Charlton T. Lewis, Charles Short, Oxford, Clarendon Press, 1879)
